answer: An AI-agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring agents to stake a deposit and earn reputation through repeated verified interactions. Each new agent must lock collateral and accumulate attestations from existing peers before its actions gain full weight, so a sybil attacker must stake real value for every fake identity, while reputation takes time and honest history to build. The pulse of ongoing work keeps glacier-sized sybil farms from growing, since every grove of identities needs constant collateral upkeep, making the attack costlier than any possible reward.
